absent: List-register value computation, fold-back, maintenance handling, and comparator policy outside configure, populate, clear, sort and summary.
Target oracle selection, affinity routing, distributor injection effects, and in-kernel irqchip presence definition.
Hardware control and list-register bit values, priority widths, and virtual machine control layouts beyond grouping described.
Reset, kick, request, cache invalidate, MMU range unmap, VNCR invalidation, and power-state transition effects.
PMU counter programming, system register access effects, and default PMU lifecycle beyond selection and installation.
Nested MMU validity, teardown blocking mode, and control-page lifetime beyond allocation and failure release.
GICv5 identifier construction, private IRQ limits, and userspace PPI mask provisioning.
Error numbers, trace payloads, and ioctl packing widths beyond field roles described.

findings.text: Exposes host-side GICv2 virtual interface control derivation for one vCPU from a pending and active summary, always enabling the interface and selecting maintenance signals for overflow conditions plus per-group indications derived from saved virtual control.

Exposes host-side GICv3 virtual interface control derivation gated on in-kernel irqchip presence, adding empty-SGI EOI count handling and a deactivation trap when host capability is absent, when active state overflows list registers, or when a VM-wide active SPI count is nonzero.

Overflow predicates compare summary counts against the global list-register count: pending overflow uses pending count alone, combined overflow uses pending plus active, and active overflow requires at least one active together with combined overflow.
Active list ordering for a vCPU requires the per-vCPU list lock on entry, snapshots virtual machine control into comparator context, then orders the list with a dedicated comparator.
List-register fill dispatch selects a version-specific helper according to global distributor type and requires the individual interrupt lock on entry.

Version-specific fill stores a computed image into the addressed per-vCPU slot and updates software interrupt state on pending indication: edge latch cleared, one SGI source consumed with latch restored while sources remain, mapped level line lowered, and a resident flag set; one version folds priority into storage while the other gates SGI source handling on emulated model.
List-register clear dispatch selects a version-specific helper by global type and each helper resets the addressed per-vCPU slot to an empty value.

Summary construction requires the per-vCPU list lock, zeroes output, walks the active list under each interrupt lock in turn, skips entries whose target oracle selects another vCPU, and increments pending versus active tallies plus an SGI tally based on identifier range.

VM IRQ-line ioctl entry decodes a packed identifier into type, vCPU selector and number, traces the request, handles CPU signals only without an in-kernel irqchip, and handles PPI and SPI injection only with one, lazily initializing the distributor, validating ranges including GICv5 private limits and userspace visibility, translating to internal identifiers, then delegating to line or distributor injection.

CPU line update maps the requested line to its virtual interrupt control bit, atomically sets or clears it, returns without further work when the level is unchanged, and otherwise records a pending-interrupt request and kicks the vCPU.
Lazy distributor initialization is a no-op once initialized, rejects non-legacy models while uninitialized, and otherwise initializes under the configuration mutex and propagates the result.

Supported vCPU feature set starts from an architected valid set and clears capabilities when host support is absent; validation rejects unknown bits, nonzero extension words, unsupported host bits, split pointer-authentication halves, strict PMU without PMU, and 32-bit combinations with MTE or nested virtualization.

Feature-change detection compares the VM-wide stored set against the incoming set, while vCPU setup provisions a default PMU when a PMU-bearing vCPU lacks one and is not strict, then initializes nested state when that feature is present.

Nested initialization requires the configuration mutex, validates an EL2 variant against host capability, ensures a zeroed per-vCPU control page, grows a VM-wide second-stage table array in fixed per-vCPU chunks with per-entry initialization, and on failure releases initialized entries and the control page before reporting.
Nested second-stage creation sizes the address range from a helper that currently returns a fixed global IPA limit.

Default PMU selection probes registered PMUs for support of the current CPU under a global mutex; installation records the PMU and a derived counter count, where the maximum is zero without a PMU, one under an imp-def trap workaround, else the general-purpose weight, and counter updates also rewrite a PMU partition field in every vCPU register view when nested support is configured.

Target programming validates target and features, takes a first-time path that rejects changes after VM-wide configuration is finalized, copies features, runs setup, resets the vCPU and marks configured plus initialized under the configuration mutex, and takes a re-init path that rejects changed features and only resets; the ioctl wrapper treats power-off as one-shot, refreshes second-stage or instruction-cache state on rerun depending on cache capability, resets interrupt controls, and publishes runnable or powered-off state under a spinlock.
Target identification maps host implementor and part readings to a small set of architected targets with a generic fallback.
VGIC list and interrupt locking requires the per-vCPU active list lock across sort and summary, with each interrupt lock held across populate and briefly per entry during summary.
Configuration mutex serializes lazy distributor init, first-time target programming, nested initialization, and PMU installation.

Stage-two teardown nests source, address-space read, and MMU write locks around per-slot plus nested unmapping, nested unmapping asserts write ownership, and vCPU power-state publication uses a dedicated spinlock.
Pending and active summary carries separate pending, active and SGI counts; per-version CPU interfaces carry a control word, a saved virtual machine control word, and an indexed list-register file.

Deactivation trapping is forced even though the relevant guest mode can change without notice and when host deactivation support is absent, trading extra traps for correctness across CPUs and for SPIs deactivated elsewhere.

Level-mapped and SGI state updates on fill mutate line level and source masks to permit new arrivals, so concurrent injection must be ordered by the interrupt lock, and stage-two slot teardown must intersect each host mapping and skip non-ordinary mappings to avoid unmapping holes.

IRQ-line ioctl encoding packs type, split vCPU selector and number fields with distinct CPU, PPI and SPI types and CPU IRQ and FIQ numbers; PPI and SPI legality uses SGI, private and shared boundaries plus GICv5 translation with a userspace-visible PPI mask.

vCPU feature and target ABI uses a valid feature mask with 32-bit, PMU, strict PMU, SVE, pointer-authentication halves, nested and power-off bits, a generic target plus implementor-specific targets, and legacy versus versioned distributor model selectors.
Exposes full second-stage teardown across all memory slots and nested tables, with per-slot host-mapping intersection handling delegated to an internal helper.
Exposes helpers reporting host CPU target, IPA bit limit, maximum PMU counters, and default PMU installation result.
